options.opa: The kinetic constant (k) decreases with increasing temperature.
options.opc: In reactions with higher activation energy (Ea), the kinetic constant (k) depends enormously on the temperature.

analysis: The Arrhenius equation describes the temperature dependence of reaction rates. The kinetic constant (k) increases with increasing temperature, as shown by the exponential term in the equation. The pre-exponential factor (A) is not necessarily dimensionless and can have units depending on the specific reaction. The kinetic constant (k) does depend on temperature, but it is not solely based on the activation energy (Ea). The pre-exponential factor (A) and the kinetic constant (k) are not inversely proportional, as they are both part of the Arrhenius equation and have a complex relationship. The Arrhenius parameters are indeed the kinetic constant (k) and the pre-exponential factor (A).
